verdict.label: STEP ASIDE — WTI Double-Test + VIX Reset + Netflix Guidance Miss
verdict.rationale_short: WTI crude tested $80+ intraday for a second consecutive session before settling at ~$79.63 — the formal daily settlement trigger was narrowly avoided again, but the two-day intraday breach pattern is the market's verdict that the $80 trip wire will not hold indefinitely. VIX climbed to 16.73 (+6.76%), moving further from the 15.00 BUY threshold and erasing yesterday's progress. Netflix Q3 guidance came in below consensus on both revenue and EPS, killing the evening bullish signal the morning brief identified as necessary for a constructive Friday. None of the three conditions for a BUY upgrade were met; the setup for the coming week deteriorates toward peak Q2 earnings risk with September hike probability approaching 60%.

The Iran Hormuz blockade — now in its fourth day — ensures July CPI (est. August 13) will carry a significant oil-shock component regardless of daily settlements. XLE provides energy FCF exposure and directly hedges the September hike repricing path. TLT short captures the 30Y stubbornly above 5.00% for five consecutive sessions. Pair: long XLE at 12% of portfolio; short TLT 5% notional.

trade_setups.invalidation: Iran-US ceasefire with Hormuz at 70%+ pre-blockade flow AND WTI below $70 for two consecutive sessions.

bear_case: Counter-thesis: the WTI double intraday test at $80 is not a settlement breach — crude settled at ~$79.63, replicating July 15's pattern of testing and failing to hold the $80 level. Two consecutive fails to hold $80 at settlement suggests $80 is resistance, not a sustained regime shift. TSMC's Q2 call produced no H2 2026 wafer-hike-effective-date confirmation, and the supply-shortage language ('extends into 2027') is unambiguously demand-bullish. NVDA staged a dramatic intraday recovery from $197 premarket to ~$208–210 — on a day when ARM fell 5% and Micron fell 8% — a relative-strength signal that the market is ring-fencing NVDA's AI positioning from the commodity-chip selloff. SPX at 7,533 holds 74 points above the 7,460 base-case support with no breadth deterioration in non-semi names (AAPL +0.33%, GOOGL flat, AMZN –0.43%). Netflix's Q3 guidance miss reflects peak content amortization timing, not demand collapse; subscribers and engagement trends remain intact. If SPX closes above 7,600 on Monday with VIX below 16, the STEP ASIDE call was too early by two sessions.
